Main.dc.html.title: Phone overview, a dry day: mosaic

s1.text:
The idea

1. Now stays on top: the temperature, and today hour by hour against the usual for this date (±7 days, earlier years).
2. One full-width feature tile, chosen by the refresh run: whatever is most unusual right now. A live rain event always wins.
3. A two-column mosaic of half-width tiles: a number, a short delta, and a mini chart that makes the comparison. No sentences, no how-to-read lines.
4. Tapping a tile zooms it into the full view, where the FT-style finding headline, the long charts and the year-over-year comparisons live.

s2.text:
Sample values throughout, not station data. Light theme only here; the tokens are the site's.

Try it: press Play on the dry-day board and tap the feature tile or the temperature tile.

s3.text:
Open questions

- What earns the feature slot on a dry day (biggest departure from normal, or a priority list)?
- Which eight tiles, and in what order?
- Zoom as a full-screen view (shown) or a bottom sheet?
- Desktop: the same tiles on a 4-column grid, the feature spanning 2x2.

History grows: a window row or tile appears only once the station's record covers it (Salmon Run, from Nov 3, shows Today, Yesterday, 7 days and Full history).

t1.text: Lookout overview: now, one feature, a mosaic of context
